hints: Remove the moduli by squaring both non-negative sides, or find the boundary points from $5x-3=\pm2(3x-7)$.
Solve the two resulting linear equations to obtain the critical values that split the real line.
Test one value in each interval in the original strict inequality, and exclude both boundary points.
walkthrough:
Square both non-negative sides to eliminate the absolute values:
$$|5x - 3| < 2|3x - 7|$$
$$(5x - 3)^2 < 4(3x - 7)^2$$

Rearrange all terms to one side to form a standard quadratic inequality:
$$0 < (36 - 25)x^2 + (-168 + 30)x + (196 - 9)$$
$$11x^2 - 138x + 187 > 0$$

Find the critical values by solving the corresponding linear equations $5x - 3 = \pm 2(3x - 7)$:
$$\text{Case 1: } 5x - 3 = 6x - 14 \implies x = 11$$
$$\text{Case 2: } 5x - 3 = -6x + 14 \implies 11x = 17 \implies x = \dfrac{17}{11}$$

Since the quadratic has a positive coefficient of $x^2$, the product is strictly positive outside the roots:
$$x < \dfrac{17}{11} \quad \text{or} \quad x > 11$$

ai_rubric.Solving Quadratic Equations: Identifies $(5x-3)^2<4(3x-7)^2$, corresponding quadratic equation, or $5x-3=\pm2(3x-7)$; Derives critical values $17/11$ and $11$; Concludes with $x<\dfrac{17}{11}$ or $x>11$.
